channel.title: Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty (rferl.org)

item.title: Recruited In Russia, Kyrgyz Men Go Missing In Ukraine -- Leaving Wives Desperate
item.description: Thousands of Central Asian families have been left searching for husbands drafted into the Russian Army and lost in the war in Ukraine, trapped between grief, bureaucracy, and silence. Their wives carry the unbearable weight of hope and fear, as well as the financial burden of making ends meet.

item.title: A Military On The Move: US Hardware Spotted Amid Iran Tensions
item.description: As US forces gather in the Middle East amid rising tensions with Iran, photographers have captured images of naval and air units on the move -- from Crete to the Azores, from Britain to Bulgaria.

item.title: Red Cross Chief Says Russia Blocking Access to Ukrainian Prisoners Of War
item.description: Nearly 200,000 requests to trace missing people have been submitted to the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) from both Ukrainian and Russian families since the start of Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, ICRC Director-General Pierre Krähenbühl told RFE/RL.

item.title: Ukraine Marks 4th Anniversary Of Full-Scale War As Russia Strikes Zaporizhzhya
item.description: Ukrainians marked the fourth anniversary of Russia’s full-scale invasion with memorial ceremonies across Ukraine. European leaders attended events in Kyiv as people reflected on the war’s toll and their hopes for peace. On the day of the anniversary, drone strikes hit the city of Zaporizhzhya.

item.title: Ukrainian Teams Fight To Recover Bodies Of Fallen Soldiers
item.description: On the fourth anniversary of the Russian invasion, tens of thousands of families of missing soldiers still waiting in the dark for news of their loved ones. Oleksiy Yukov, the head of a frontline body recovery team, explains why its so important to him to bring back the remains of the fallen.

item.title: Iran Arrests Japan Public Broadcaster's Bureau Chief In Tehran
item.description: Iran has arrested the bureau chief of Japan's public broadcaster, NHK World, and transferred him to Tehran’s notorious Evin Prison, two sources told RFE/RL's Radio Farda.

item.title: Student Protests Continue To Spread Across Tehran
item.description: University students across the Iranian capital turned out for a fourth day of renewed anti-government protests on February 24, following a brutal state crackdown in January. Thousands of people were killed last month in protests sparked by economic collapse and oppression in Iran.

item.title: In Record-Breaking Address, Trump Warns Iran, Vows Ukraine Peace
item.description: US President Donald Trump used the longest State of the Union address in US history to repeat the threat of military action against Iran if diplomacy fails -- and pledged to keep negotiating to end the war in Ukraine.

item.title: Popular Iranian Actor Flees Homeland After Deadly Crackdown On Protests
item.description: Iranian actor Amirali Danaei has left Iran, denouncing the Islamic republic as a dictatorship after a deadly crackdown on protests. Once a state-TV star, he now vows never to work under the clerical system again, calling the crisis a human tragedy where “human lives are not up for negotiation.”

item.title: In State Of The Union Address, Trump Vows To Block Iran's Nuclear Ambitions
item.description: US President Donald Trump delivered his State of the Union address before a joint session of Congress on February 24. As a US military buildup continues in the Middle East, raising fears of a conflict with Iran, Trump said that he will "never allow" Iran to acquire a nuclear weapon.
